answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can ration sponsorship like saffron: each established agent may vouch for only one newcomer per epoch, and the vouch locks part of its own stake until the newcomer passes three graded rounds. Sponsors are drawn at random from an atlas of the trust graph that excludes the newcomer's invite tree. A farm of a hundred fake heads therefore needs a hundred unrelated sponsors willing to risk bonded stake, and each exposed fake slashes its sponsor's bond, an onyx-hard cost that honest newcomers never trigger.
